note: Jones Creek RV Campground at Danish Alps SRA, on the hill above the west shore of 219-acre Kramper Lake near Hubbard. 50-amp electric pads (water at most) in a herringbone, plus basic sites; most sites look over the lake across the park road. Some sites reservable on ReserveAmerica, the rest first-come (self-pay). Showers, dump and fish-cleaning station. The separate Pigeon Creek Equestrian Campground (horse campers, corrals) is on the south peninsula ~1.1 km away. Park entry permit required. --Claude
summary: The stored pin and its lakefront evidence describe the wrong campground. The pin sits by the Pigeon Creek Equestrian Campground, the herringbone on the south peninsula. The RV campground, Jones Creek, is the herringbone on the hill ~1.1 km north: RA GIS points, NAIP imagery and Campendium's point agree. From Jones Creek the lake is 120-150 m off, across a second loop and the park road, so the call goes down lakefront -> lakeview. RA confirms 50 A and water hookups, showers, dump, 180-day booking and some FCFS sites. RA's phone is (402) 632-4109, not the grid's 402-755-2284.
flags: PIN MOVE (~1.1 km): stored 42.37364,-96.58308 is south of the equestrian campground. RA GIS for the 11 reservable Jones Creek RV sites runs 42.3814-42.3848 / -96.5812..-96.5829, and the NAIP herringbone centre is ~42.3838,-96.5821 (Campendium 42.382647,-96.581719). Suggest 42.3838,-96.5821.

WATERFRONT CHANGED lakefront -> lakeview. The old evidence (herringbone 'on a peninsula nearly surrounded by lake') describes the Pigeon Creek Equestrian Campground. Jones Creek's pads sit on the hill 120-150 m from the shore. Between them and the water are a second loop road with buildings and the park road along the shore, so they are not on-water. RA tags every site 'Near Water - no'. A Campendium reviewer says 'almost all have view of lake' (219-acre Kramper Lake).

NOT A SPLIT: the Pigeon Creek Equestrian Campground is a separate place ~1.1 km south (RA GIS 42.3741-42.3759) with its own access off the south park road. It is a horse campground (corrals, an equestrian loop on RA; NGPC says 14 corrals). That is out of scope under the curation rules, so no entry. A 2021 Campendium reviewer did camp there in an RV at $35. If AWH would take a horse loop open to any RV, it is the lakefront one.

PHONE CONFLICT: RA lists (402) 632-4109 (VisitNebraska the same per search snippet). The NGPC 2025 grid lists 402-755-2284, and a search snippet cites the 2026 State Parks Guide at 402-632-4106. Suggest (402) 632-4109 (the booking site's own). apply.py doesn't write phone.
